figures.before: Base Flood Elevation: What It Is, How to Read a FIRM Panel, How It Sets Your Minimum Finished Floor
figures.alt: Coastal home elevated foundation with reinforced concrete piers, structural beams, and open site access below the floor framing
figures.caption: Flood-zone construction begins with the finished-floor requirement and the system that supports it. Elevation, foundations, utilities, access, enclosure limitations, drainage, and the structural load path must work together.

figures.before: Duval County Floodplain Management: Local Amendments More Restrictive Than FEMA Minimum Standards
figures.alt: Industrial site grading with a stormwater basin, controlled slopes, compacted subgrade, and clear perimeter access
figures.caption: Floodplain compliance is also a site problem. The project team needs to consider grading, drainage, water path, utilities, access, permits, elevation documentation, and the local requirements that apply to the parcel.

figures.before: The Substantial Improvement Rule: 50% Threshold and What "Full Code Compliance" Means
figures.alt: Elevated coastal home under construction with reinforced concrete piers, floor framing, weather-resistive barrier, and a clean northeast Florida site
figures.caption: When a project crosses a major compliance threshold, the construction approach may need to respond to the whole building and site condition rather than treating the work as an isolated renovation decision.
